{{Term/Store|Ganon's Castle||Series, OoT, OoT3D, TWW, TWWHD}},{{Exp Game|OoT, TWW}}<ref>{{Cite Book|quote= |book= E |publisher= |page= 149 {{Exp Game|OoT}} & 153 {{Exp Game|TWW}}}}</ref> also known as '''Ganon's Tower''', or '''Ganon's Fortress''', {{Exp Game|OoT, TWW}}<ref>{{Cite|Link...can you hear me? It's Rauru, the Sage. We six will gather our power to create a bridge to the castle where Ganondorf dwells... The castle's keep, which is known as Ganon's Tower, is protected by six evil barriers. Bring down the six barriers and save Princess Zelda!!|Rauru|OoT}}</ref><ref>{{Cite|Long ago, Ganon's Tower was an impenetrable fortress that not even the daring and dauntless Knights of Hyrule could hope to assail.|King of Red Lions|TWW}}</ref> is a recurring {{Term|Series|Dungeon|link}} in {{TLoZ|Series}}.

==Overview==
==={{OoT|-}}===
====Entrance to {{Term|OoT3D|Ganon's Castle}}====
In {{OoT}}, its prime association, Ganon's Castle is the final [[Dungeons in Ocarina of Time|dungeon]] in the game and [[Ganon]]'s stronghold, and replaces [[Hyrule Castle]] over the seven years that [[Link]] sleeps in suspended animation after he withdraws the [[Master Sword]] from its [[Pedestal of Time|pedestal]]. Although its exterior can be explored as early as Link becomes the [[Hero of Time]], the dark castle floats over a large lake of magma, rendering it inaccessible until the [[Sage#Ocarina of Time|Six Sages]] are awakened and create a [[Rainbow Bridge|colorful bridge of light]], allowing Link to enter '''Inside Ganon's Castle'''.
[[File:OoT Rainbow Bridge.png|thumb|288x288px|Once the Six Sages are awakened, Link is able to enter Ganon's Castle via the Rainbow Bridge]]

====Themes and Navigation====
[[File:Ganonscaaastle.jpg|thumb|290x290px|right|The magical barriers protecting the inner part of Ganon's Castle]]
Within the tower's center is a giant spindle leading up to the top that is blocked off by a surrounding magic seal. The powerful force field that surrounds the spindle is powered by six colorful barriers that are based on each of the adult [[Dungeon|Dungeons]]. Above each of the barriers is the [[Symbols#Sage Emblems|Sage symbol]] that represents the element. At the end of each room lies the source of the barrier's energy, requiring [[Light Arrow|Light Arrows]] to destroy them and seemingly freeing the respective Sage inside.

Ordered counterclockwise, the routes are:

*'''Forest Barrier''': Actually a [[wind|wind-themed]] route, it revolves around collection of [[Silver Rupee]]s over endless pits ventilated by fans, and a fight against [[Wolfos]].
*'''Water Barrier''': Actually an [[ice|ice-themed]] route, it revolves around pushing [[block]]s on a slippery, icy floor and using [[Blue Fire]] to melt red ice.
*'''Shadow Barrier''': It revolves around crossing a prolonged chasm by activating some passages and walking through invisible platforms. The [[Golden Gauntlets]] are found in this room.
*'''Fire Barrier''': It revolves around collecting Silver Rupees across a huge room with lava while avoiding obstacles and enemies. The Golden Gauntlets are required here.
*'''Light Barrier''': It can only be accessed after the huge boulder blocking it is removed with the Golden Gauntlets, and revolves around exploring various small rooms, each one showing a different puzzle. Notably, the barrier's core is behind a fake wall.
*'''Spirit Barrier''': It revolves around collecting Silver Rupees while avoiding [[Blade Trap]]s, a [[Light Beam]] puzzle, and the use of rare items like [[Bombchu]]s and [[Fire Arrow]]s.

There is a secret room under the bridge that contains various [[Business Scrub]]s and [[fairy|fairies]], which can become helpful as Link dispels each of the barriers in Ganon's Tower. Once the six barriers have been disintegrated, the magical barrier will disappear, allowing Link to make his way up to the castle's tower.
[[File:OoT Link in Ganon's Castle.jpg|left|thumb|271x271px|Link inside the castle's inner tower, leading to a staircase]]
The way up to the castle's inner sanctum is a long staircase that leads to increasingly more dangerous rooms filled with a pair of [[Dinolfos]], [[Stalfos]], and even [[Iron Knuckle (Boss)|Iron Knuckle]]s, which Link must defeat individually to progress up the tower. At the top awaits [[Ganondorf]], the Evil King, who is patiently waiting for the Hero of Time as he plays his own theme song on an organ while [[Princess Zelda]] remains trapped in a [[crystal]] above him. After Ganondorf is defeated in a heated battle, he destroys the throne room's ceiling in a [https://noproblo.dayjo.org/zeldasounds/OOT/OOT_Ganondorf_Yell.wav fit of rage] before falling face down, seemingly dead. The tower then begins to rumble, as the archvillain purposely intends to ultimately make his entire castle collapse to kill his foes under the rubble via his powerful dark magic, forcing Link and Princess Zelda to escape the building within a three minute time limit (which Link will be forced to restart from the top if it reaches zero at the cost of one [[Heart Container|Heart]] in damage).<ref>{{Cite|Link, listen to me! This tower will collapse soon! With his last breath, Ganondorf is trying to crush us in the ruins of the tower! We need to hurry and escape!|Princess Zelda|OoT}}</ref> All of the main doors of the castle have been blocked, and as such, it is up to the princess to use her powers and open up each of the alternate exits. The two take a long path that winds in and out of the castle, fighting enemies and dodging falling debris. Once the duo safely make it out, running for their lives, the castle itself fully collapses in front of them, with the tower sinking first followed by the rest into the foundation as well. When the destruction ends, Link and Princess Zelda believe they finally achieved victory. However, their archenemy Ganondorf, still alive, furiously appears among the ruins and transforms himself into his true form, Ganon, using the [[Triforce of Power]]. Link must defeat the massive beast once and for all to restore peace to [[Hyrule]] and accomplish his legendary title as the Hero of Time.

=====''Master Quest''=====
The mini-dungeons corresponding to each temple have been remixed in the {{MQ}} version of the game. Also, instead of two [[Beamos]] there are a [[Blade Trap]], two [[Green Bubble]]s, two [[Armos]] and an Iron Knuckle in the first room. 

*'''Forest Barrier''': The first room is identical. In the turbine room, there are now more Beamos and also an Armos. The [[Song of Time]] must be played several times.
*'''Fire Barrier''': Most platforms are moving or either rise or sink when Link stands on them. There are two big rocks now, and the Silver [[Rupee]]s are in places that are difficult to reach.
*'''Water Barrier''': In the first room, there are several stalactites that fall from the ceiling, and the blue fire is surrounded by a pillar of water. Curiously, there is a lone [[Dead Hand]]'s hand that is used to "reveal" the location of a switch hidden inside a wall that lowers the pillar of water when hit. In the second room there are three [[Keese]], each one is different. There is a Silver Rupee puzzle and more red ice.
*'''Shadow Barrier''': There are now some invisible platforms and a Beamos. The Golden Gauntlets are no longer found here, and [[Fire Arrow]]s are required to solve some puzzles.
*'''Spirit Barrier''': In the first room, instead of Silver Rupees there are some stone thrones blocking access to a switch. Some [[Fire Keese]] and a [[Torch Slug]] are found here, and there is an eye on the wall that if shot, makes an Iron Knuckle appear so the thrones can be destroyed. In the second room there are now Green Bubbles, [[ReDead]]s and [[Gibdo]]s. There are several suns, just like in the original version. However, one makes a [[Wallmaster]] appear, others make chests with replenishment appear and the last one makes the chest with the Golden Gauntlets appear. The sun required for opening the door is blocked by the Spirit Symbol on the wall and only a small portion of it can be seen.
*'''Light Barrier''': In the first room, there is a puzzle involving torches that must be lit quickly to make a chest appear over the door. The next room is the same, but instead of having to collect Silver Rupees, it is now required to activate a switch while avoiding the boulder and a Beamos. In the fake barrier room, there are no enemies, but there is a switch that gives access to the last room hidden inside a torch.

=====Small Keys=====
*In the original, there are two small keys in the light section.
*In Master Quest, there are three in the forest, shadow, and spirit sections.

==={{TWW|-}}===
[[File:WW ganontower.jpg|thumb|242x242px]]

====Entrance to Ganon's Tower====
'''Ganon's Tower''' is the last dungeon in {{TWW}} and [[Ganondorf]]'s true stronghold, and is located underneath the [[Great Sea]] in the now-forgotten land of [[Hyrule]].<ref>{{Cite|Long ago, Ganon's Tower was an impenetrable fortress that not even the daring and dauntless Knights of Hyrule could hope to assail.|King of Red Lions|TWW}}</ref> Link, the Hero of Winds, gains access to it after the [[Master Sword]] retrieves its full power and the [[Triforce#Triforce of Courage|Triforce of Courage]] is complete. When these two conditions are met and Link goes back to Hyrule Castle to ensure the safety of [[Princess Zelda]] ([[Tetra]]), he realizes that Ganondorf kidnapped her and fights two [[Mighty Darknut|Mighty Darknuts]]. Afterward, the Hero of Winds goes outside and breaks the barrier that made the Evil King's lair previously inaccessible.

The path to Ganon's Tower is full of enemies such as [[Peahat]]s, [[Moblin]]s, and even [[Darknut|Darknuts]], although they can all be easily avoided. Some chasms have to be crossed with the [[Hookshot]] as well.

====Themes and Navigation====
Once inside the tower, Link will find himself in a room with five doors. The main door leading deeper into the tower is initially blocked off by a magic seal. As such, the young hero must explore the areas behind the four remaining doors. Each area is based on one of the four main dungeons, and they all require the extensive use of its respective main dungeon item. In clockwise order, the routes are:

*'''[[Dragon Roost Cavern]]:''' It revolves around crossing a large sea of lava. There are several items that are helpful for that purpose, including [[Deku Leaf]], [[Grappling Hook]], and [[Ice Arrow]]s.
*'''[[Forbidden Woods]]:''' It revolves around crossing an endless pit with the help of movable platforms and tongue-shaped elevators.
*'''[[Earth Temple (The Wind Waker)|Earth Temple]]:''' It revolves around running through a prolonged passage guarded by undead enemies. Occasionally, the young hero must find a way to keep some switches pressed.
*'''[[Wind Temple]]:''' It revolves around crossing a wind-operated obstacle while dodging an airborne [[Wizzrobe]]. Items like [[Deku Leaf]], [[Iron Boots]] and [[Hookshot]] are required.

At the end of each mini-dungeon, Link must once again defeat its corresponding [[boss]] in order to dispel a part of the barrier (respectively, [[Gohma]], [[Kalle Demos]], [[Jalhalla]] and [[Molgera]]). Once all of the four bosses have been defeated, the seal blocking off the door to the inner part of the dungeon will be broken. Notably, the rooms leading up to the boss rematches gradually turn grayscale in color the closer it gets to the boss door, and their battle themes are slightly different, implying that the rematches are flashbacks.

Next is a puzzle room of sorts where Link can both open a quick exit to the [[Forsaken Fortress]] and enter a maze where [[Phantom Ganon]] confronts him incessantly; in the end, the young hero finds the [[Light Arrow]] upgrade, which defeats Phantom Ganon once and for all. This causes the phantom to leave [[Phantom Ganon#Phantom Ganon's Sword|its sword]] behind that Link must use to bust open a solid wall, leading to a room with a long flight of stairs infested with Moblins and Mighty Darknuts. After dispatching each of these enemies with the help of the Light Arrows, Link pushes past a large door, and enters an extremely high and wide room with a flooded floor where Princess Zelda sleeps on a bed, guarded by Ganondorf. Here, Link fights [[Puppet Ganon]], who transforms into multiple shapes in three phases. After victory, Link climbs the room to finally reach the fortress's roof to fight Ganondorf once and for all to prove his title as the Hero of Winds.

Just like the rest of Hyrule, Ganon's Tower is completely flooded after King [[Daphnes Nohansen Hyrule]] makes his wish using the [[Triforce]].

==Trivia==
[[File:OoT Phantom Ganon painting.png|thumb|265x265px|The pictures of the Forest Temple's boss room has a silhouette of Ganon's Castle]]
*In early development, Ganon's Castle was originally going to be the only setting for {{OoT}}, with the game structured similarly to [[mariowiki:Princess_Peach's_Castle|Princess Peach's Castle]] in ''[[mariowiki:Super_Mario_64|Super Mario 64]]'', and various different rooms in the castle itself serving as the [[Dungeons in Ocarina of Time|dungeons]]. Although the original plot was scrapped in the final release, the [[Forest Temple]] has leftover elements of this. The dungeon's architecture resembles a dark castle unlike all other Temples, and the six paintings in the [[boss]] room where [[Phantom Ganon]] comes in and out actually shows Ganon's Castle in the background.
*Fittingly, the background music of Ganon's Castle's tower area in {{OoT|-}} and Ganon's Tower in {{TWW}} are [[Ganon]]'s own [[Recurring Music in The Legend of Zelda Series|theme song]].
*When [[Link]] enters the tower section of Ganon's Castle and [[Ganondorf]] is heard playing his theme song on a pipe organ, the music grows louder as the hero goes higher up toward the throne room.
*The scene of Link escaping the destruction of Ganon's Castle with [[Princess Zelda]] in ''Ocarina of Time'' is widely considered one of the most unique in terms of gameplay in the series (or most [[Final Boss]] battles in general), as it occurred between the first and second phases against both of Ganon's [[Gerudo]] and [[Demon]] forms at the title's final battle, respectively, giving a rather harrowing or exciting experience.
*Ganon's Castle in ''[[The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 3D|Ocarina of Time 3D]]'' has a different design from the original game where it has gargoyle statues on its sides and the overall structure appears more demonic with spikes and closer to a fortress, similar in akin to [[mariowiki:Bowser's_Castle|Bowser's Castle]] from the [[Mario (franchise)|''Mario'' franchise]], which the castle itself is a parallel to.
**It also bears some resemblance to the architecture of several of [https://lotr.fandom.com/wiki/Sauron Sauron]'s fortresses from the Tolkien [https://lotr.fandom.com/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings ''The'' ''Lord of the Rings''] franchise, most notably Barad-dûr.
*Unlike other dungeons in {{OoT|-}}, Ganon's Castle has two background themes. One is used for its first floor to break the barrier and the other for the tower leading to Ganondorf (not including [[Fire Temple]] based on different release versions).
*According to an artwork of {{OoT|-}}, Ganondorf and Link are shown directly battling each other at hand-to-hand combat. This suggests this was originally planned for the actual duel in-game, but was changed to a [[Dead Man's Volley]] similar to Phantom Ganon's late in development (which is met with criticism by some fans). However, Ganondorf can perform an Earthquake Punch if the hero were to stand under him, in which this attack by the villain cannot be blocked with a [[Shield]].
*Despite {{TAoL}} have dungeons being completely covered by boulder when completed and ''[[The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past|A Link the Past]]'' have some large walls being blown open by explosions, Ganon's Castle in {{OoT|-}} is the first time in [[The Legend of Zelda (series)|{{TLoZ|-}} series]] where any form of buildings is shown collapsing on-screen.
*In the original [[Nintendo 64]] version of {{OoT|-}}, colored energizes can be seen flowing on the exterior of the castle during the escape, and in the cutscene where it ultimately collapses, they fade out and turn gray.
*During and after the collapse of the castle, due to Link and Princess Zelda taking the alternate exit, the [[Rainbow Bridge]] disappears. In the [[The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Himekawa)|manga adaptation]] by [[Akira Himekawa]], however, they seemingly used the main entrance and bridge to escape.
*If Link attempts to play the "[[Sun's Song]]" at the exterior of Ganon's Castle, time itself is restricted to only daytime due to Ganon's power. It is completely ineffective when he is inside the stronghold. It's presumed by some players that had it been nighttime, the environment, especially during the final battle, would become too dark.[[File:OoT Ganon's Castle roof collapsing.png|thumb|284x284px|Link looking around as the walls of the throne room collapse from Ganondorf's power]]
*At Ganondorf's apparent defeat by Link in the castle's throne room, the Gerudo warlock, in a fit of anger, unleashes a powerful wave of energy that results in the top of Ganon's Castle suffering an earthquake and then being obliterated, but the hero himself remaining unaffected. It is likely the [[Triforce of Courage]] protected the [[Hero of Time]] from his archenemy's magical explosion.
**Strangely, the broken floor from the Dead Man's Volley duel is seen completely restored in the cutscene leading to the escape with Princess Zelda. It is unknown what caused it to occur.
**In the Himekawa manga adaptation for the game, Ganondorf's last ditch effort is toned down to him simply yelling upward and yelling "No!!!" before apparently collapsing dead, with the overall structure of the throne room remaining intact before the collapse, with Ganondorf's seeming corpse being showed to be buried by the rubble. Similarly, his Earthquake punch during the duel was toned down to him simply managing to make a crack in the floor rather than obliterating the perimeter outright.
*The act of Ganondorf kidnapping Princess Zelda and tells Link to rescue her at his stronghold in {{OoT|-}} and {{TWW|-}} is a parallel to the traditional goal of [[Mario]] and [[Luigi]] having to save [[Princess Peach]] from [[Bowser]] in the ''Super Mario'' games.
*Ganon's Castle in {{OoT|-}} and its remake notably has clouds floating around the top of its tower section like that of a ring, similar to [[Death Mountain]] as well as [[Woodfall]] in {{MM}}. It is visible in official artwork and even in the background of the destroyed [[Hyrule Castle Town|Hyrule Castle Town Market]].
*Ganon's Castle/Tower is the setting of the Final Boss battle of {{OoT|-}} and {{TWW|-}}, respectively.
*The Forest and Water Barriers of Ganon's Castle are the only ones not to stay akin to its temple theme. Instead of having forest and water-type challenges, they instead incorporate wind and ice elements, with the water barrier having rooms similar to that of the {{Term|OoT3D|Ice Cavern|link}}. This is due to the developmental version of each temple being wind and ice based respectively.{{Fact}}
*Although Ganon's Castle in {{OoT|-}} is also known as "Ganon's Tower", it and the one from the ''Wind Waker'' are completely different architectures. Ironically, [[Ganon's Tower]] from {{aLttP|-}} has the ''Wind Waker'' counterpart reuse a similar structure.[[File:OoT Ganon's Castle orange fog.png|thumb|257x257px|The entrance of the tower area of Ganon's Castle using the orange fog seen at Ganondorf's throne room in {{OoT|-}} via debug cheats]]
*The interior redesign of Ganon's Castle in ''Ocarina of Time 3D'' and especially the following final battle has received criticism for lacking the dark atmosphere seen in the original release. This is primarily due to the Nintendo 64 (and other [[wikipedia:Fifth_generation_of_video_game_consoles|32-bit era]] home consoles) known to use [[wikipedia:Distance_fog|Distance Fog]] for its lighting effects because of processing power limitations and it can change color based on certain areas or attacks by some [[Boss|bosses]] (this can easily be seen with ROM hacking). The [[Nintendo 3DS]], despite being significantly more technologically advanced, does not have such a graphical mechanic, and therefore often appears rather bright.
**This is also the case for the game's direct sequel, {{MM|-}} and its [[The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask 3D|remake]].
*When viewed from the [[Gallery:Hyrule#Four_Swords_Adventures|World Map]] in ''[[The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures|Four Swords Adventures]]'', the [[Temple of Darkness]] resembles the original design for Ganon's Castle.
*Needless to say, the speed of the [[wikipedia:Progressive_collapse|progressive collapse]] of Ganon's Castle during Link and Princess Zelda's escape is unrealistic in comparison to real-world cases of large buildings failing, as it is very slow.
**Strangely, the [https://noproblo.dayjo.org/zeldasounds/OOT/OOT_GanonsTower_Fall_Loop.wav sound effect of the tower section of Ganon's Castle collapsing] in {{OoT|-}} is similar to large doors closing.
**If {{OoT|-}} is played on the [[IQue Player]] or modern emulators including [[Nintendo]]'s Virtual Console or [[Nintendo Switch Online]], due to the increased framerate of 60fps rather than 30 from the N64's processing power, the sound of the castle's collapse falls out of sync as its tower crumbles to the ground. This also applies to Ganondorf's transformation into Ganon.
*There is a graphical texture error on the blueish top part of the wall between and inside the Fire and Light Barriers at the main room. It is massively stretched and distorted, appearing to have a zigzag-like pattern.
*The plot of {{TP}} featuring Ganondorf sealing Hyrule Castle in a barrier, where the area is inaccessible by Link until the end of the game, is similar to Ganon's Tower in {{OoT|-}} and especially {{TWW|-}}. This would make sense, as this game is confirmed to have taken many beta elements from the N64 title.
*The Forest, Spirit, Shadow, and Fire Barriers had doors with bars in the original and ''[[The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Master Quest|Master Quest]]''.
**The Water Barrier had doors with bars in the original and one locked door and another door with bars in ''Master Quest''.
**The Light Barrier had two locked doors and one door with bars in the original and ''Master Quest''.
*Like Ganon's Tower or the [[Dark World]] in {{aLttP|-}}, due to Ganon's powerful dark energy, the weather at Ganon's Castle and the nearby Hyrule Castle Town Market is of a thunderstorm without rain, and crashes of lightning occur during the final battle against the Demon King himself.
*During the battle against Ganondorf in {{OoT|-}}, for unknown reasons, it is possible for the [[Hookshot]]/[[Longshot]] to latch itself to the walls of the entire throne room.
*Sometimes missed by players, during the final battle in {{OoT|-}}, when Ganon attacks and destroys a piece of his castle's ruins to make [[Magic Jar|Magic Jars]], [[Bomb|Bombs]], [[Deku Nut|Deku Nuts]], [[Arrow|Arrows]], or [[Fairy|Fairies]] appear to aid Link, a [https://noproblo.dayjo.org/zeldasounds/OOT/OOT_Ganon_Smash.wav sound effect of clanging metal] can be heard.
*In ''Ocarina of Time 3D'', skulls of monsters with spears on their eye sockets can be found at the exterior area of Ganon's Castle, indicating a fierce battle between Hyrule and Ganon's forces during the take over of [[Hyrule Castle]]. In the original game, skulls are indeed present, but lack any spears.
*In the infamous [[SpaceWorld 2000 GameCube Tech Demo]], although it is unknown what exact location Link and Ganondorf are in while they are battling each other in a one-on-one sword fight, due to the environment being a dim castle hall, it is presumed to be Ganon's Castle.
*The four dungeon rooms' unique themes within Ganon's Tower in {{TWW|-}} are a combination of the original dungeons and Ganon's theme.
*The theme song of the escape from Ganon's Castle is heard in the [[Failed Execution of Ganondorf|failed execution of Ganondorf]] in ''Twilight Princess'' when the villain broke free from his chains with the [[Triforce of Power]] and killing one of the ancient [[Sage|Sages]].
